source: hmm Ventures classifier methodology (IM §2.2, §5.1). Worked examples drawn from the canonical 9-exit dataset and the off-mandate exclusions in the doctrine.

t1.label: T1. Licence-as-barrier
t1.rule: Company cannot legally operate without regulatory approval. The classifier flags T1 when registry, product description, or hiring signals indicate dependence on a named licence, clearance, or certification regime in one of the four markets.

examples.rule_applied: Telehealth licensing + ACHS accreditation. Cannot prescribe or dispense without approved-provider status.
examples.outcome: Exit 2026 — Hims & Hers, up to $1.15B total.

examples.rule_applied: TGA + FDA medical-device clearance. Cannot ship breast-density AI without regulatory approval per indication.
Virtual specialist care licensing. Cannot deliver specialist consults without registered-practitioner credentialing.

t2.label: T2. Compulsion-as-barrier
t2.rule: Buyers are statutorily required to purchase compliant solutions. The classifier flags T2 when sector and customer profile map to a compliance mandate that creates demand for the company's product.

examples.rule_applied: AU Building & Construction Industry Security of Payment Act compels head contractors to manage statutory progress claims. The buyer's purchase is the compliance mechanism.
FSANZ Standard 3.2.2A compels food businesses to demonstrate supply-chain traceability. Buyers can only source from compliant growers.
Renewable Energy Target compels retailers to source from accredited generators. Buyers must purchase from licensed renewables to meet statutory targets.

excluded.label: Excluded. Off-mandate.
excluded.rule: Fails both T1 and T2 screens, or sits inside an off-mandate sector. Cross-cutting band is restricted to AI and Data only; financial services / fintech and defence tech are off-mandate everywhere.

examples.rule_applied: Financial services / fintech is fully off-mandate. Banking licences are real T1 barriers, but the sector itself sits outside the fund's scope.
examples.outcome: Excluded — off-mandate sector, regardless of regulatory depth.

examples.rule_applied: Defence-tech is off-mandate everywhere. Export-control regimes meet the T1 criterion in form, but the fund does not invest in defence applications.
No named licence, clearance, or certification dependency. Buyers are not statutorily required to purchase. Fails both screens.
